fi-centromochlus-perugiae.title: Honeycomb Tatia
fi-centromochlus-perugiae.summary: The oil catfish, Centromochlus perugiae, is a small auchenipterid catfish from Peru and Ecuador. It lives around the shorelines of swift-flowing rivers with sandy substrates and no aquatic plants. By…
rows: Insectivorous in the wild, but in aquaria it relishes live and frozen foods such as bloodworm, earthworms etc., as well as sinking dried foods.
notes: The fish like to squeeze themselves into spaces little bigger than themselves during the day, so provide plenty of hiding places among tangles of bogwood or lengths of plastic piping.
A sand substrate is best, and the fish prefer a good amount of water flow, although this isn't absolutely essential.

fi-megalechis-thoracata.title: Hoplo Catfish
fi-megalechis-thoracata.summary: The spotted hoplo, Megalechis thoracata, is a callichthyid catfish widespread across northern South America, living primarily in still waters. Still widely referred to as Hoplosternum thoracatum, it…
notes: The hoplo is not a particularly shy catfish but will still appreciate some cover in the form of rocks, plants and bogwood .
Water flow should be slow or still, although the fish will adapt to stronger conditions.

fi-oxydoras-niger.title: Ripsaw Catfish
fi-oxydoras-niger.summary: The ripsaw catfish, Oxydoras niger, is a large doradid catfish from many of the major river systems of northern South America. Reaching 90 cm, it is only for the experienced fishkeeper and best…
rows: Found throughout many of the major river systems of northern South America .
notes: Will appreciate cover in the form of rockwork, roots and bogwood .
Plants can also be used but ensure plenty swimming space is also provided.

fi-phractocephalus-hemioliopterus.title: Redtail Catfish
fi-phractocephalus-hemioliopterus.summary: The red-tail catfish, Phractocephalus hemioliopterus, is a giant pimelodid catfish from much of the Amazon and Rio Orinoco basins in South America. The largest specimen recorded by science measured…
rows: Carnivore / micropredator. Quite an opportunistic feeder in nature, feeding on fish, invertebrates and fallen fruits.
Present throughout much of the Amazon and Rio Orinoco basins in Colombia , Venezuela , Guyana , Ecuador , Peru , Bolivia and Brazil .
notes: Strictly speaking, decor isn't necessary for a tank containing an adult, provided the lighting is fairly dim.
You can however add some large chunks of bogwood , beech branches or smooth rocks if you wish.

fi-sorubim-lima.title: Lima Shovelnose Catfish
fi-sorubim-lima.summary: The duckbill catfish, Sorubim lima, is a pimelodid catfish recorded from rivers across South America, including the Amazon, Orinoco and Paraná. It is also known as the 'hockey stick catfish' and…
rows: Almost exclusively carnivorous preying on smaller fishes, crustaceans, invertebrates, etc.
A very widespread species that has been recorded from Venezuela, Ecuador , Colombia, Peru, Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay , Uruguay and Argentina.
notes: This species is nocturnal and a dimly-lit tank with substrate of soft sand suits it best.
Other décor need consist only of some decent-sized roots and branches which can be arranged to form sheltered areas although plants can also be added should you wish.

fi-agamyxis-pectinifrons.title: Spotted Raphael Catfish
fi-agamyxis-pectinifrons.summary: The spotted talking catfish, Agamyxis pectinifrons, is a doradid catfish from the Amazon basin in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia and Peru. Very common in the trade, it is hardy and relatively long-lived,…
rows: group of 4 or more specimens, though can be maintained individually if you wish, and it will also group together with similarly-looking relatives such as Platydoras armatulus , Acanthodoras spinosissimus , and Amblydoras hancockii .
Omnivore. This species is an omnivorous generalist and will accept most commonly-encountered prepared and frozen foods.
The type locality is given as 'Pebas, Equador' by Cope (1870), but this apparently refers to the settlement of the same name located east of the city of Iquitos in Loreto Region,…
notes: Best maintained in a dimly-lit set-up with a soft, sandy substrate and plenty of cover in the form of aquatic vegetation, tangles of driftwood or artificial caves of some kind.
Bright lighting isn't really appreciated since this species is largely nocturnal by nature.

fi-liosomadoras-morrowi.title: False Jaguar Catfish
fi-liosomadoras-morrowi.summary: The false jaguar catfish, Liosomadoras morrowi, is an auchenipterid catfish from the Río Ucayali basin in Peru. It is often confused with its congener L. oncinus, from which it differs in its duller…
notes: This is a nocturnal fish, so dim lighting is required to make it feel secure.
Plenty of cover should also be provided, particularly if you're keeping several fish together.
